title: A fresh idempotency key is made per click, and the selection survives a failed or stale refund, so a second click refunds the same orders again
evidence: app.js:128 calls newIdempotencyKey() inside every refundSelected() run. state.selected is cleared only inside load() (app.js:98) after a successful fetch. On failure the catch at app.js:131-133 leaves state.selected and the enabled 'Refund N orders' button untouched. api.js:32 and README.md:9 say the key exists so a repeated request for the same attempt is ignored; a new key per click defeats that.
failing_case: 1) Select 3 paid orders, confirm. POST /refunds succeeds. 2) The follow-up GET /orders fails (offline, 502) or the refund response is lost on the network. 3) The table still shows 'paid', the button still reads 'Refund 3 orders' and is enabled. 4) The user clicks again and confirms; a new UUID is sent, the server cannot match it to the first attempt, and the money goes back twice. The only guard is a line of text telling the user to check statuses first.
remediation: Clear state.selected (or mark those ids as pending) as soon as the refund call resolves. Keep one key per selection attempt and reuse it on retry until the server confirms; only mint a new key when the selected set changes.

title: No refund eligibility rule: already-refunded, pending and unknown orders can be ticked and sent for refund, and the confirmation counts their totals
evidence: renderRow (app.js:34-60) gives every row a checkbox regardless of order.status. selectedOrders() filters only by selection. refundSelected (app.js:119-123) sums o.total for all of them and asks 'This sends money back to the customers.' domain.js has no refund-eligibility function. No requirement is stated in the files, so this rests on the obvious meaning of status 'refunded'.
failing_case: Filter 'All', tick one order whose badge says 'refunded' (total $80) and one 'paid' order ($20). The dialog says 'Refund 2 orders totalling $100.00', and both ids are POSTed. If the server does not reject the already-refunded id, $80 is refunded twice; if it does, the whole batch may fail with a generic 'refund was not confirmed' and the user cannot tell which order caused it.
remediation: Add a pure canRefund(order) in domain.js (status === 'paid'), disable the checkbox for other statuses, compute the confirmed amount from the eligible set, and test it. Keep the server-side check too.

requirement.why: The status value 'refunded' implies the order has already been refunded; no document states the eligibility rule.

title: Paging is silent for screen-reader users and the pager button that was just used can become disabled under the keyboard focus
evidence: index.html:34 puts the page label in a plain span with no live region. app.js:71-72 set prev/next disabled in the same render that replaces all rows, and nothing moves or restores focus. README.md:5 says the interface was not tested with a screen reader.
failing_case: A keyboard user on page 2 of 3 presses Next. Rows change, the label reads 'Page 3 of 3' with no announcement, and the Next button becomes disabled while focused, so focus is dropped in browsers that blur disabled controls and the user has to Tab back from the top.
remediation: Make the page label role=status (or add a polite live region), and when a pager button disables itself, move focus to the other pager button or the table caption.

title: The page title sits 24 px left of the content column on wide screens
evidence: The h1 box is 1100 px wide and centred with no inner padding (styles.css:23). main is also 1100 px wide but with 24 px padding (styles.css:24), box-sizing border-box, so its content starts 24 px further in. At 1360 px the h1 starts at x=130 and the stats tiles at x=154.
failing_case: Open at 1360 px: the 'Orders' heading and the first tile edge do not line up.
remediation: Give the h1 the same horizontal padding as main (padding: 0 24px with the 1100 px cap), or wrap both in one container class.
